paragraph.text: consideration for animals doesn't depend on utilitarianism. Equal consideration is a formal principle: it says we shouldn't be biased when weighing each individual's interests, whatever theory we use to decide what to do. Utilitarians, rights theorists, contractualists, egalitarians and capabilities theorists disagree about almost everything, and even so they have arrived at the rejection of speciesism. Knocking down utilitarianism doesn't rescue animal exploitation.
"All this animal rights talk comes from Peter Singer, who's a utilitarian. And utilitarianism justifies horrible things."
The main argument for considering animals comes from Peter Singer's utilitarianism.
Utilitarianism has unacceptable consequences, such as allowing an innocent person to be sacrificed to benefit many.
A conclusion that depends on a false theory isn't justified.
So the case for considering animals isn't justified.

fails at P1: consideration for animals is defended by theories that reject utilitarianism.
"The sentience criterion only makes sense in a utilitarian ethics."

Imagine three teachers who disagree about how to share a cake: one wants to give more to whoever is hungriest, another wants equal slices, another wants to draw lots. But all three agree you can't leave a child without cake just because they have red hair. It's similar with animals: people who study ethics disagree about many things, but many agree it isn't fair to let someone suffer just because they belong to another species.

It isn't. Tom Regan defended rights and was a harsh critic of utilitarianism. Martha Nussbaum uses the capabilities approach. Mark Rowlands uses contractualism. They all reach the same conclusion: animals count. In 2022, more than 500 philosophers from different schools signed the Montreal Declaration condemning animal exploitation. If you think utilitarianism is wrong, pick another theory. Speciesism is still left without a justification.
"Which ethical theory do you think is correct? Let's see what it says about making animals suffer without need."
Who counts and how to weigh without bias
Equal consideration is compatible with any theory that isn't biased. Utilitarianism is only one of them.

The rejection of speciesism has been defended by rights theories (Regan), contractualist ones (Rowlands), the capabilities approach (Nussbaum), virtue and care ethics, among others. See the overview in "The state of the art in animal ethics", in the Beyond veganism section.

text.bold: 2. Rival theories agree on the conclusion.

paragraph.text: Imagine two rescued animals and two ways of sheltering them. The utilitarian picks the one that maximizes the total good, the maximin supporter picks the one that improves the situation of whoever is worst off, the egalitarian picks the one that reduces inequality. All of them keep the same decision if the individuals swap places. Whoever changes the decision only because of species is no longer following any of these theories.

text.bold: 3. Knocking down a theory doesn't confirm the opposite conclusion.

paragraph.text: Even if utilitarianism were false, an argument for speciesism would still be needed, and that argument is still missing (A8).

text.bold: 4. The argument attacks the person, not the thesis.

Utilitarianism has serious problems, discussed for over a century, and it's true that
